entities.summary: Capital of ancient Egypt during the Old Kingdom (c. 2686–2181 BCE) and the administrative center of Egypt for much of its history, located at the apex of the Nile Delta near modern Cairo. Founded by Menes (Narmer), the unifier of Upper and Lower Egypt, Memphis was home to the great temple of Ptah, the Saqqara necropolis (including the Step Pyramid of Djoser), and a cosmopolitan population that included foreign traders, diplomats, and craftsmen. The "Memphite Theology," inscribed on the Shabaka Stone, preserves one of the most sophisticated theological compositions from the ancient world.
